title: Time Complexity Big-O Check
description: Classify growth rates and dominant terms from the lesson.

questions.prompt: Nested loops `for i in 0..n` and `for j in 0..n` with a tiny body are typically:
questions.explanation: Nested loops over `n` × `n` → `O(n²)`, even if the body is tiny. Big-O tracks growth of work with `n`.

questions.prompt: Two sequential full passes over an array of length `n` are still classified as:

options.text: `O(2n)` which is a different class from `O(n)`

questions.explanation: Big-O ignores constants and lower-order terms: `2n` is still `O(n)`. Focus on the dominant term.

questions.prompt: Halving the search space each step (binary search style) is typically:
questions.explanation: Halving `n` each step (binary search style) → `O(log n)`.

options.text: How runtime grows as input size `n` grows
How much RAM the OS reserves at startup
The number of comments in the function

questions.explanation: Big-O describes how runtime grows as input size `n` grows. It is about growth, not absolute milliseconds on your laptop.
